messages:
Maya Patel: ran side-by-side tests between replay harness and synthetic loadgen for /v1/embeddings-rerank (redwood-embed-1.0-q4_0). big p99 gap when synthetic used, esp batch>=12.

Leo Kim: paste the exact commands and runner config?

Maya Patel: here:
```
# synthetic
./loadgen --endpoint /v1/embeddings-rerank --mode synthetic --qps 450 --concurrency 48 --batch-size 16 --vector-dim 1024 --seq-dist uniform --model redwood-embed-1.0-q4_0 --kernel-select auto --continuous-batcher off

# replay
./loadgen --endpoint /v1/embeddings-rerank --mode replay --trace traces/replay_2026-03-01.json --concurrency 32 --model redwood-embed-1.0-q4_0 --kernel-select auto --continuous-batcher off
```
Synthetic p99 ~590ms, replay p99 ~220ms. medians match.

Anita Zhao: hypothesis: kernel-selector fallback + low KV prefix locality in synthetic. Synthetic randomizes prefixes -> low prefix-hit -> more memcpy/serialize work; also batch packing differs.

Maya Patel: KV stats: replay prefix-hit 80%, synthetic 18%. Flamegraphs uploaded: https://perf.internal/fg/17890

Rick Owens: quick experiments:
- force kernel-select=optimized -> synthetic p99 ~245ms
- force kernel-select=generic -> synthetic p99 ~640ms
Kernel diff explains ~400ms. KV delta ~30-60ms.

Jess Carter: Need apples-to-apples. Synthetic should match seq-len dist and interarrival times and candidate-count distribution. Otherwise batcher and scheduler decisions differ and we get misleading regressions.

Leo Kim: try continuous-batcher=on and pinned-alloc. Also run --kernel-select {auto,optimized,generic} + --kv-debug + --mem-profile.

Maya Patel: continuous-batcher=on + pinned-alloc improved synthetic p99 from 410ms->270ms at batch=16; replay improved 220->200ms. Added synthetic-replay profile that samples seq-len/interarrival/candidate-count from trace; that converges p99 to within 10-20ms of replay.

Anita Zhao: root causes:
- kernel-selection heuristics pick generic kernel under many partial/diverse batches
- low prefix locality => KV misses and extra memcpy
- packing heuristics produce more partial batches under uniform seq-dist

Rick Owens: mitigations:
- tighten kernel-selection thresholds to favor optimized kernel unless specific layout detected
- prefer prefix-aligned packing where safe
- enable continuous-batcher default for rerank endpoint
- micro-opt KV memcpy path to avoid unnecessary host-device copies

Jess Carter: test matrix to validate:
- vector dims: 512/1024
- candidate counts: 1/10/50
- payload: JSON/protobuf
- batch sizes: 1/8/16/32
Record p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU util, prefix-hit, kernel breakdown, memcpy time %.

Maya Patel: will add perf job with these knobs and upload artifacts. Opening PRs for perf profile, kernel-selector tweak, and KV memcpy patch. PerfBot: queued job #1012 on perf-runners. :robot_face:
